subject: Sales follow-up: Multilingual model evals & next steps (EU/APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@globexretail.de>, Kenji Sato <k.sato@tonari.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sales follow-up: Multilingual model evals & next steps (EU/APAC)

Hi Anna / Kenji —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs
- Support for customer-facing search & summarization across DE/FR/ES (EU) and JA/KO/EN-APAC locales
- High-throughput inference with sub-300ms token latency for short responses (~50 tokens)
- Strong quality parity across locales; you called out DE product descriptions and JA customer chat specifically

Recommended immediate actions
1) Share a small prompt set (we can run a lightweight eval): I attached a recommended prompt_set_eu_apac.csv template.
2) Run a focused benchmark on 2-3 candidate models across your representative prompts. We suggest testing: 
   - redwood-rlhf-4b-quant (cost-efficient baseline)
   - open-llama-13b-int8 (higher quality on EU languages in our internal tests)
   - redwood-qa-7b-mt (multi-lingual fine-tuned variant for QA/summarization)

3) We'll run an internal baseline and return an initial_eval_results_summary.pdf with per-locale BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics + human-sampled quality notes.

Logistics / timeline
- If you can drop the prompt set by EOD Wed (your timezone), we can have initial numbers back by Fri.
- After numbers: schedule a 30-min call to go over model choices + cost/latency tradeoffs.

Benchmark links I mentioned:
- Public benchmark dashboard: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/globex-multilingual-2027
- Shared eval folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-assets

Attachments: prompt_set_eu_apac.csv (template)

Thanks — happy to adjust model list if you have internal constraints (on-prem, quantization limits, etc.).

Best,
Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@globexretail.de>

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 13:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Sales follow-up: Multilingual model evals & next steps (EU/APAC)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. This looks good. A couple of clarifications from our side: 
- For data residency reasons, anything that touches EU customer PII needs to be tested on our EU-located staging (we can share a temporary dataset with anonymized fields).
- For Japanese (JA) chat, we prioritize politeness/formality and correct honorifics — can that be part of the human sampling rubric?

We will:
- Drop the prompt_set_eu_apac.csv filled with ~150 examples (mix of product descriptions, customer chat snippets, and search queries) into your Drive folder by Wed EOD CEST.
- Share a brief access ticket if you need to run on our EU staging.

One ask: can you also include a quick note about regression risk when switching quantization profiles? We had an issue last year with a model that dropped accuracy after going to int8.

Talk soon,
Anna
Head of AI Product | Globex Retail
anna.mueller@globexretail.de | +49 30 1234 5678
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@globexretail.de>
Cc: Kenji Sato <k.sato@tonari.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sales follow-up: Multilingual model evals & next steps (EU/APAC)

Hi Anna — great, thank you. Quick answers inline and next steps: 

- EU staging: understood. If you provide temporary staging credentials/ingest ticket, our Dedicated/private team can run the eval on EU-hosted infra. For hosted testing we can also queue jobs in eu-central-1.

- Honorifics & politeness: we'll add explicit scoring buckets in the human-sample rubric for JA (politeness, honorific correctness) and DE (gendered language sensitivity where relevant).

- Quantization/regression note: short version below (I'll ask Neha to add a technical appendix):
   * Quantization can reduce numeric precision leading to subtle output shifts, especially for inflection-rich languages (DE) and politeness-sensitive languages (JA).
   * Best practice: run head-to-head evals (FP16 vs int8) on your prompt set and surface both automated metrics and human-rated quality.
   * We often retain a small FP16 tail for locale-critical routes (can be configured as a routing policy to fall back to higher-precision variant on low-confidence or specific locales).

Next steps:
- Neha (cc'd) will take point on the technical appendix and will attach an initial_eval_results_summary.pdf and a model recommendation spreadsheet once we run the baseline.
- Can you confirm who on your side should get the Drive folder invite and whether we should expect PII-sanitized CSVs or a secure S3 share?

I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up for next Monday unless you prefer earlier.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Looping in with the promised technical appendix and initial attachments.

Attached (stubs):
- initial_eval_results_summary.pdf — includes per-locale automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE proxies we use internally), inference latency table, and human-sample notes (10 samples per locale).
- redwood_model_recommendation.xlsx — cost/latency/quality tradeoffs and suggested rollout policy (canary FP16 tail for DE/JA).
- prompt_set_eu_apac.csv — filled template from Globex (sanitized).

Key technical highlights (summary):
- On our pilot run across the provided prompt set (150 examples): redwood-qa-7b-mt and open-llama-13b-int8 showed similar automated scores for EN/ES, but for DE and JA the multi-lingual fine-tuned redwood-qa-7b-mt had better human-rated fluency and formality control.
- Quantization impact: open-llama-13b-int8 saw a 3-5 point drop in human-rated accuracy on JA honorifics vs its FP16 baseline; for DE the drop was smaller but visible on morphological correctness.
- Recommendation: run a short live A/B with traffic routing by locale: int8 for general EN/ES traffic; FP16 fallback for DE/JA critical routes.

I'll push the full appendix and the benchmark artifacts to the shared Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-assets

Neha Kapoor
Applied ML — Model Evaluation Lead | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
